title: The island two countries fought over with bottles of booze
hook: Canada and Denmark fought over an island by leaving each other booze.
summary: Canada and Denmark disputed tiny Hans Island for decades, trading flags and bottles of alcohol, until they split it in 2022.
sources: Encyclopaedia Britannica / Wikipedia 'Hans Island': 1973 Canada-Denmark border treaty left the island undecided; 1984 Canadian soldiers left a flag and Canadian Club whisky; Danish minister Tom Høyem left schnapps and a note.
BBC / Reuters, June 2022: Canada and Denmark agreed to split Hans Island, creating a new land border.

lines.text: Canada and Denmark fought over an island by leaving each other booze.
lines.caps: *Canada | and *Denmark | fought over *an island | by leaving *booze

lines.text: Hans Island is a barren rock between Greenland and Canada.
lines.caps: *Hans Island | is a barren *rock | between *Greenland | and *Canada

lines.text: A nineteen seventy-three border treaty skipped it, so both claimed it.
lines.caps: A *1973 | border *treaty | *skipped it, | so both *claimed it

lines.text: In nineteen eighty-four, Canadian soldiers landed and left a flag and whisky.
lines.caps: In *1984, | Canadian *soldiers | *landed and left | a *flag and whisky

lines.text: Denmark's minister then arrived, and left a Danish flag and schnapps.
lines.caps: Denmark's *minister | then *arrived, | left a *Danish flag | and *schnapps

lines.text: His note welcomed visitors to the Danish island.
The swapping went on for decades.
In twenty twenty-two, they split it almost in half.
It became a land border settled politely.

post.caption:
Two countries argued over a rock for decades and used bottles, not bullets.
Which bottle would you have left on the island?
